title: Where should I start?
answer: Start in Real-data study. Expand Landing window to enter alternative arrival times in UTC, then set Surface duration and Ranking priority. Open Advanced settings for the original coordinates and landing time, plus terrain, power and communication requirements. Select Run study. The search is bounded to the Connecting Ridge study footprint. NASA maps opens the source layers.

title: Real or simulated data?
answer: Real-data study uses archived NASA LOLA terrain and long-term screening maps with SPICE DE421 geometry for your selected dates. It is not live imagery. NASA percentages describe a long-term modeled cycle, not sunlight hours for your mission. Simulated demo uses fictional sites and illustrative values. Keep those modes distinct.

title: How do comparisons work?
answer: Run a study, then choose R1, R2 or R3 above the terrain, or Inspect R1, R2 or R3 in Compare. The left inspector and shared mission timeline update together. Compare candidate opens the detailed original/alternative table. The timeline aligns hours since each landing; UTC dates can differ. Lower/upper cases express terrain sensitivity, not guaranteed confidence bounds. Earth visibility is a geometric opportunity, not a proven radio link.

title: Is a qualifying site safe?
answer: Meets assessed limits does not mean safe to land. Ground strength, footpad sinkage, rocks, plume effects, thermal behavior and trajectory reachability remain unassessed. There is no universal best site. This assistant cannot execute searches or choose an optimal site: enter your location, UTC times and requirements in the study form, run the calculator, and review its actual results.

title: What does the terrain map show?
answer: The real study covers a 5 by 5 km Connecting Ridge patch. Switch from 3D terrain to NASA maps to see sunlight, Earth visibility, permanent shadow and LOLA terrain layers. Click the map or enter original coordinates in Advanced settings. The hillshade is calculated from elevations, not a photograph. Screening pixels are 60 m; regional elevation is 5 m, and patch checks are 50 m. The 3D display samples at 50 m without changing analysis. Footpad-scale hazards remain unresolved.

title: How do themes and field help work?
answer: Use the Light or Dark button in the top bar to switch themes. Your choice is saved on this browser when local storage is available. Small circled question marks explain controls and results on hover, keyboard focus or tap. Press Escape or move focus away to dismiss a tip. Advanced settings holds the detailed scientific inputs.

title: Why is the search slow?
answer: A first uncached real-data search can take a minute or more. Wait for its progress indicator; only one analysis runs at a time. Repeating identical inputs can reuse verified cached results. HTTP 429 means the service is busy or a request limit was reached: wait before retrying. If the service is unavailable, use the saved presentation report or the clearly labeled simulated demo.
